newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore changes public housing mortgage policy.
newsitem.headline: Singapore changes public housing mortgage policy.

text.p: The Singapore government on Saturday said it had revised its mortgage financing policy for the purchase of Housing Development Board (HDB), or government-subsidised, flats.
It said it will change the basis for computing interest rates to a monthly basis from the current six-monthly.
The government has also set new credit assessment criteria designed to help buyers keep their purchases within their financial means.
The government will limit to two the number of subsidised housing loans for which flat-buyers are eligible regardless of whether the flats are bought direct or from the resale market.

For the third and subsequent housing loans obtained from the HDB, flat-buyers and transferees will be charged a market interest rate. This rate will be pegged to the government-owned post office savings bank housing interest rate.
In another move, the government said buyers of new flats and transferees of existing flats must use all of their central provident fund savings before new housing loans will be granted to them.
Currently buyers of resale flats only are required to use central provident fund (CPF) money fully, and the change means this is being extended to buyers of new HDB flats.

The government has also abolished subsidised interest rates for buyers and transferees if their monthly househould income exceeds Singapore $8,000, and if they already own private residential, commercial or industrial properties.
The new measures apply immediately to all new applicants and existing applicants of new HDB flats, buyers of HDB resale flats and transferees, with some exceptions.
The exceptions include those who are have been short-listed to book their flats.
The government said that the objective of the changes is to bring its mortgage financing policy for public flats closer into line with private sector market practice.
On Friday, property share prices fell sharply in Singapore in anticipation of HDB changes tightening the public housing market.

Analysts said any changes to the public housing market would have an impact on private housing prices as the two markets are linked, and profits from the one are sometimes used to finance investment in the other. -- Singapore newsroom 65-870380
